video_title: Money Forcing Major Changes For The Thunder?

quotes.speaker: Brian Windhorst
quotes.summary_phrase: Oklahoma City Thunder's massive 2026 offseason salary cap projections
quotes.excerpt: they would be somewhere in the neighborhood of $260 million

text_blocks.speaker: Brian Windhorst
text_blocks.text: If they right now draft the two picks they have and pick up all the team options they have for Isaiah Hartenstein and Lu Dort and Kenrich Williams, they would be somewhere in the neighborhood of $260 million. And Bobby Marks, our guy, has it at $264 million, which is plus tax.

text_blocks.speaker: Bobby Marks
text_blocks.text: Right. That's not only that's just their payroll number. So that is not only into the second apron, it is $42 million over the second apron.

quotes.speaker: Bobby Marks
quotes.summary_phrase: Oklahoma City Thunder's critical team option decisions for key players
quotes.excerpt: Kenrich Williams either not be on the Thunder or not be playing on the Thunder

text_blocks.speaker: Bobby Marks
text_blocks.text: You have those three main team options to deal with. Those are the biggest things. You have Kenrich Williams just over $7 million. Kenrich Williams either not be on the Thunder or not be playing on the Thunder for a $7 million option next year. That seems very simple. Lu Dort, who is on a $17.7 million team option for next season, I think that is an interesting conversation. And then Isaiah Hartenstein, who is on a $28.5 million team option.

text_blocks.speaker: Brian Windhorst
text_blocks.text: You know who else thinks it's an interesting conversation? Lu Dort, who hired Rich Paul in the middle of this last season.

quotes.speaker: Bobby Marks
quotes.summary_phrase: Isaiah Hartenstein's likely contract extension with the Oklahoma City Thunder
quotes.excerpt: I would guess that what will end up happening there is he will sign a longer-term deal

text_blocks.speaker: Bobby Marks
text_blocks.text: Isaiah Hartenstein has this $28.5 million team option and I would say of those three guys, he is the most likely guy to be back. However, I would guess that what will end up happening there is he will sign a longer-term deal for a lower number because the Thunder have some ability to handle those negotiations with that team option and get Hartenstein some longer-term money and also lower their bill for this upcoming season.

text_blocks.speaker: Brian Windhorst
text_blocks.text: They could pick up Hartenstein's option and just say we'll see you in September. Or they could say, Isaiah, can we come to terms on a new deal and here is where this new deal could start. They are allowed to negotiate that right now.

quotes.speaker: Bobby Marks
quotes.summary_phrase: Potential trade scenarios involving Lu Dort to reduce team salary
quotes.excerpt: You're saying trade Dort into space without taking back salary

text_blocks.speaker: Bobby Marks
text_blocks.text: If they trade Dort and trade Kenrich Williams, if they trade those two guys, and sign Hartenstein for a deal that starts at $20 million, they've already lapped off $35 million off of that number I was talking about and then they're $5 million over the second apron.

text_blocks.speaker: Brian Windhorst
text_blocks.text: You're saying trade Dort into space without taking back salary. Which I'm sure they could do. I think that could be done.

quotes.speaker: Bobby Marks
quotes.summary_phrase: Lu Dort's vital role as a culture and defensive leader
quotes.excerpt: Lu Dort is tied with Shai Gilgeous-Alexander as the longest tenured active members of the Oklahoma City Thunder

text_blocks.speaker: Bobby Marks
text_blocks.text: You do have to consider the human element of all this. Lu Dort is tied with Shai Gilgeous-Alexander as the longest tenured active members of the Oklahoma City Thunder. He is the ultimate culture guy there, developmental success story, coming in as an undrafted free agent, working his way into being a quality starter for a championship team. And while Shai made a very public show of saying I'm not going to be involved at all in these discussions, I'm going to let the best GM in the world do his job, just trust me on this, Shai will lobby for Lu.

text_blocks.speaker: Brian Windhorst
text_blocks.text: Of course he will. It's his team Canada teammate, longtime teammate there, they're good friends. It only makes sense.

quotes.speaker: Bobby Marks
quotes.summary_phrase: Cason Wallace's potential for an expanded role next season
quotes.excerpt: Cason Wallace could step right in to that starting lineup and be an all defensive selection

text_blocks.speaker: Bobby Marks
text_blocks.text: They have ready-made replacements. Like Cason Wallace could step right in to that starting lineup and be an all defensive selection as a point of attack defender. He's maybe you could argue even an upgrade as a defensive player as great as Lu Dort is on that end of the floor with more offensive upside for sure. AJ Mitchell, maybe they decide to plug him in to the starting lineup and really add another dynamic playmaker there as they did in the playoffs.

text_blocks.speaker: Brian Windhorst
text_blocks.text: Is AJ Mitchell eligible for an extension?

text_blocks.speaker: Bobby Marks
text_blocks.text: He's got one year plus a team option, yeah.
